findings.title: Removal listener now gated on V1 only: V2 resources are orphaned and V1+V2 together throws
findings.body:
The role/client/group removal listener now runs only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. This has two consequences.

1. With only V2 enabled, deleting a client never cleans up its admin-permission resource. That resource is named after the client id and lives in the admin-permissions client. Any scope permissions referencing it are left dangling, so stale grants and resources accumulate.

2. When V1 and V2 are both enabled, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`. `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, so the `ClientRemovedEvent` handler fails and client deletion breaks.

The listener should check which version is active. For V2 it should remove or detach the V2 resources/permissions instead of calling the V1-only API.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-clients resource is missing
findings.body:
When no per-client resource exists, `hasPermission` falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`. That method can return null, for example when the schema is not supported for the server or the 'Clients' resource is absent in a realm initialized before this type was added.

The null is passed straight to `findByResource(server, resource)` and later dereferenced via `resource.getScopes()`. The result is an NPE instead of a clean `false`. A null check is needed, matching what the sibling `hasPermission(String)` does.

findings.title: Existing realms never get the new Clients resource/scopes
findings.body:
`init()` returns early if the admin-permissions client already exists. Scopes and type resources are created only on first initialization.

Realms that were initialized before this change therefore lack the new scopes (`configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`) and the 'Clients' all-resource. In those realms, `getOrCreateResource` for a client throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")`. Creating all-clients permissions also cannot work.

A migration or idempotent sync of schema scopes and resources is needed.

findings.title: getResourceName not extended for Clients type
findings.body:
`getResourceName` maps user resources to usernames and the type resource to "All users". There is no equivalent branch for the new Clients type.

As a result, client permissions display the raw internal client UUID, or 'Clients' for the all-resource, instead of the clientId or "All clients". This makes permission listings confusing.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports
findings.body:
Several pieces of `ClientPermissionsV2` are never used:
- the private method `getEvaluationContext`
- the `logger` field
- the imports `Scope` and the static `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`

They appear to be copied from V1 and should be removed.
